::: {.incremental}
- Define accounting
- Identify generally accepted accounting principles
- Cite examples of accounting concepts and principles
- Solve exercises on accounting principles
:::

## What is Accounting? {auto-animate="true"}

::: {.framework-box}
::: {.framework-item}
**I**dentifying
:::
::: {.framework-item}
**R**ecording
:::
::: {.framework-item}
**C**ommunicating
:::
:::

# Fundamental Concepts {transition="convex"}

## Business Entity Concept {transition="fade" transition-speed="fast"}

::: {.concept-card}
Business is separate from owner

::: {.example-box}
**Example:** Owner's personal expenses ≠ Business expenses
:::
:::

## Going Concern Concept {transition="fade" transition-speed="fast"}

::: {.concept-card}
Business continues indefinitely

::: {.example-box}
**Example:** Asset depreciation spread over useful life
:::
:::

## Periodicity {transition="fade" transition-speed="fast"}

::: {.concept-card}
Financial statements in equal time intervals

- **Calendar Year:** Jan 1 - Dec 31
- **Fiscal Year:** Any 12-month period
:::

## Monetary Unit Concept {transition="fade" transition-speed="fast"}

::: {.concept-card}
All transactions in peso terms

::: {.example-box}
**Example:** Hiring employees not recorded (no monetary value)
:::
:::

## Accrual Basis Concept {transition="fade" transition-speed="fast"}

::: {.concept-card}
- Revenue: recognized when <span class="highlight">earned</span>
- Expenses: recognized when <span class="highlight">incurred</span>

::: {.example-box}
**Example:** Services rendered = revenue (even if unpaid)
:::
:::

# Basic Principles {transition="convex"}

## The Six Principles {transition="fade" transition-speed="fast"}

::: {.principle-grid}
::: {.principle-item}
**Objectivity**
Supported by evidence
:::
::: {.principle-item}
**Cost**
Original acquisition cost
:::
::: {.principle-item}
**Full Disclosure**
All relevant information
:::
::: {.principle-item}
**Matching**
Costs match revenues
:::
::: {.principle-item}
**Consistency**
Uniform approaches
:::
::: {.principle-item}
**Materiality**
Focus on important info
:::
:::

# Application {transition="convex"}

## Case 1: Business Entity {transition="fade" transition-speed="fast"}

**Mrs. Labandera's expenses:**

| Item | Amount | Include? |
|------|--------|----------|
| Health Insurance | ₱15,000 | No |
| Rent Expense | ₱35,000 | Yes |
| Home Utilities | ₱8,000 | No |
| Store Utilities | ₱12,000 | Yes |
| Withdrawal | ₱30,000 | No |

<div style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 1.5em; color: #27ae60; font-weight: 700;">
Total Business Expenses: ₱47,000
</div>

## Case 2: Accrual & Matching {transition="fade" transition-speed="fast"}

::: {.concept-card}
**Ocean Deep Resort:**

- Received ₱150,000 advance payment
- When recognize revenue? <span class="highlight">When service rendered</span>
- When recognize expenses? <span class="highlight">Match with revenue period</span>
:::

# Exercise

## Problem {transition="fade" transition-speed="fast"}

::: {.concept-card}
**Mr. Castro's A&Z Aquatic Fishes - February 2021**

Revenue: ₱150,000 | Recorded expenses: ₱100,000
:::

| Expense | Amount |
|---------|--------|
| Aircon Repair (residence) | ₱12,000 |
| Life Insurance | ₱15,000 |
| Rent Expense | ₱20,000 |
| Home Utilities | ₱4,800 |
| Store Utilities | ₱5,200 |
| Salaries | ₱35,000 |
| Family Dinner | ₱8,000 |

## Solution

::: {.concept-card}
**Business Expenses:**

- Rent: ₱20,000
- Store Utilities: ₱5,200
- Salaries: ₱35,000

<div style="margin-top: 20px; font-size: 1.5em; color: #27ae60;">
✓ Total: ₱60,200
</div>

<div style="margin-top: 20px; font-size: 1.5em; color: #2980b9;">
📊 Net Income: ₱89,800
</div>
:::
